title: Count Inversions Using Merge Sort
statement:
Given an array of N integers, count the number of **inversions**: pairs (i, j) where i < j and A[i] > A[j].

An inversion is a measure of how far the array is from being sorted.

**Algorithm**: Modify merge sort — during the merge step, when an element from the right half is placed before remaining elements of the left half, those are all inversions. Add the count of remaining left-half elements at that point.

Total complexity: O(N log N).
inputFormat:
Line 1: a single integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer: the total number of inversions.

starterCode.python:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

def merge_count(arr):
    if len(arr) <= 1:
        return arr, 0
    mid = len(arr) // 2
    left, lc = merge_count(arr[:mid])
    right, rc = merge_count(arr[mid:])
    # Write merge step here, counting cross inversions
    merged = []
    count = lc + rc
    i = j = 0
    while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
        pass  # your logic here
    return merged + left[i:] + right[j:], count

_, total = merge_count(a)
print(total)
